chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

'There are those among us who claim that the word of God, Mighty and Majestic, "So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know" [16:43], refers to the Jews and the Christians.' He said: 'In that case, they would be calling you to their religion.' He said, placing his hand upon his chest: 'We are the People of the Reminder, and we are the ones to be asked.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ: People of the Reminder — those who preserve and transmit divine knowledge; in Shia tradition, identified exclusively with the Imams of the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.الْمَسْئُولُونَ: The ones to be asked — those possessing authoritative religious knowledge that others must consult
key_terms.يَزْعُمُونَ: They claim/allege — connotes a doubtful or erroneous assertion

ai.seo_question: Who are the People of the Reminder (Ahl al-Dhikr) in Quran 16:43 according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) responds to a misinterpretation of Quran 16:43 in which some Muslims claimed that 'the People of the Reminder' refers to the Jews and Christians. The Imam refutes this by pointing out the logical absurdity: if Jews and Christians were the intended reference, they would invite Muslims to their own religions. The Imam then places his hand on his chest and declares that the Imams of the Ahlulbayt are the true 'People of the Reminder' — the authoritative religious guides whom God commanded Muslims to consult. This hadith is part of a chapter establishing the Imams as the proper interpreters of the Quran and the religious authorities to whom the community must turn.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘There are ones with us who are alleging that the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [16:43] so ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know, they are the Jews and the Christians’. Heasws said: ‘Then they would be calling you to their religion’. He (the narrator) said, ‘Heasws said by (placing) hisasws upon hisasws chest: ‘Weasws are the Ahl Al-Zikr (People of the Reminder), and weasws are to be asked’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala‘ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who ha said that he said the who has said the following to abu Ja‘far ( a.s.).

“These are people who think that the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. ‘Ask the people of Dhikr if you do not know,’ refers to the Jews and the Christians.” The Imams (a.s.) asked, “Do they call you to their religion?” He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) has aid that the Imams (a.s.) “Said, with his hand (pointing) to his chest, ‘We are the People of Dhikr (reminders of Allah) and we are the ones who must be asked questions.’”
